meaning: back at the beginning, usually because something failed and you have to start again
example: We lost the file, so we are back to square one.
origin: Possibly from old board games, where square one was the starting square

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a game and win first place
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about starting again, not about winning or finishing first.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to draw a perfect square on paper
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal idea of a shape, not the idiomatic meaning about going back to the start.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to become very angry with someone
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has no connection to anger; it describes returning to the beginning of a process.

explanation: 'Back to square one' means returning to the very beginning, often after a plan fails. It is used in everyday English when progress is lost and work must start again.
